# Module `base64`

base64 - RFC 4648 §4 encoding/decoding, in pure Vyb.

Standard alphabet (`A-Za-z0-9+/`), `=` padding, byte-for-byte over a String.
The runtime already ships `vyb_base64_encode` for the WebSocket handshake
(stdlib/websocket), but that intrinsic is one-way and handshake-scoped; this
module is the general, portable surface a program reaches for when it needs
base64 for a data URL, a receipt field, or an artifact envelope.

  import base64::{b64_encode, b64_decode}
  b64_encode("foobar")            -> "Zm9vYmFy"
  b64_encode("f")                 -> "Zg=="
  b64_decode("Zm9vYmFy")          -> "foobar"
  b64_decode("Zm9vY")             -> absent (not a whole number of groups)

Encoding is byte-oriented: `char_at(i) & 0xFF` for every input byte, so binary
Strings (embedded NULs, high-bit bytes) round-trip unchanged. Decoding is
strict on purpose -- it rejects a non-multiple-of-4 length, characters outside
the alphabet, and `=` anywhere but the final one or two positions, rather than
silently returning a truncated value.

<a id="sym-b64_decode"></a>
### `b64_decode` · fn

```
b64_decode(s<String>)<String?> ->
```

RFC 4648 §4 decode of `s`. Absent (`String?()`) when `s` is not a well-formed
base64 group stream: length not a multiple of 4, a character outside the
alphabet, or `=` in a position other than the last one or two. Valid input
round-trips with `b64_encode`.

### `b64_encode` · fn

```
b64_encode(data<String>)<String> ->
```

RFC 4648 §4 base64 of `data`, padded. Every input byte is consumed; the tail
group is padded with `=` as the spec requires.

The 6-bit value of alphabet character `c` (a byte code), or -1 if `c` is not in
